title: Going Camping
goal: Find your reserved campsite, ask about facilities and current rules, and request supplies.

runs.text: is an area with camping sites. A
is an individual place to camp. An
is a van equipped for camping.
are facilities you can ask about.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: Hi, we have a campsite reservation under Alex Chen for two nights.

turns.en: Hi, we have a campsite reservation under Alex Chen for two nights.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Is that for a tent or an RV?

turns.en: Is that for a tent or an RV?

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: A tent. Where should we set up?

turns.en: A tent. Where should we set up?

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: Can we park our car at the site?

turns.en: Can we park our car at the site?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: In this campground, use the marked parking space beside it.

turns.en: In this campground, use the marked parking space beside it.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: And where can we get drinking water?

turns.en: And where can we get drinking water?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: At the water station next to the camp store.

turns.en: At the water station next to the camp store.

blocks.caption: Arrive and locate the site · Camper & Host

runs.text: means arrange your camping place and equipment.
means finish the stay. Ask “What time do we need to leave the site?” rather than assuming hotel checkout rules apply.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: There's a fire restriction today. No campfires.

turns.en: There's a fire restriction today. No campfires.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Let me check the current rules for that type of stove.

turns.en: Let me check the current rules for that type of stove.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: Please do. Where can we read the posted rules?

turns.en: Please do. Where can we read the posted rules?

blocks.caption: Ask about fires and equipment · Camper & Host

runs.text: Ask about current restrictions instead of relying on a previous visit. The National Park Service's Zion campground guidance explicitly directs visitors to current fire restrictions and a ranger or camp host. This example does not prescribe stove use or the rules of another park.
, small sticks for lighting a flame;
, material providing energy. Different stoves use different fuel, so “Do you sell fuel for this stove?” is more precise than naming any container as suitable.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: We forgot our flashlight. Do you sell one?

turns.en: We forgot our flashlight. Do you sell one?

turns.speaker: Clerk

runs.text: Yes. This one takes two batteries.

turns.en: Yes. This one takes two batteries.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: Okay, I'd like the flashlight and the matching batteries.

turns.en: Okay, I'd like the flashlight and the matching batteries.

blocks.caption: Buy what you forgot · Camper & Clerk

runs.text: You can also ask “Do you have matches?” or “Where are the trash bins?” “We forgot…” gives the reason; it does not require a long apology. With a companion, “Let's set up first, then explore” organizes the plan. “I'm not up for a long hike tonight” expresses a real limit.
Fictional campground card: tent site 14; two nights; showers opposite the site; water next to the store; checkout noon; campfires prohibited today; stove restrictions require confirmation.
Check in. Partner asks tent or RV, then gives the site. Confirm its location and ask about water.
Ask about a campfire. Partner states the restriction. Ask about your stove without deciding the answer yourself.
Buy a flashlight. Partner says batteries are not included. Say what you want to purchase.
Tell a companion your first two actions. Change the plan if you are tired.
Solo: read each host or clerk turn and create your camper replies. Later describe the campground with the card hidden.

“Site fourteen, across from the showers?” “Could you confirm the rule for this stove?” “Let's set up, then get water.” Check whether you locate the site and distinguish an allowed activity from a rule still needing confirmation.
Source note: Current-rule approach informed by [National Park Service campground guidance](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/camping-regulations.htm); the campground itself is invented.
